title: Cutting at the group's lowest bottom brings back the round-5 slab-on-a-slope bug whenever a lower solid touches the house
detail: _cut_level cuts every member of a connected group at max(plan_level, the group's lowest bottom). If a solid touching the house goes lower than the house (steps or a terrace down a slope), the house is cut at the grade plane, which is below its own slab. Its section is empty, so it drops out of 'at the main grade level'. That is the exact round-5 case (house slab at 2.75 ft, grade plane 2.0 ft) that 7f8fca8 fixed and the test test_a_slab_above_the_grade_plane_on_a_slope_is_cut_at_its_own_bottom pins. Its docstring calls it P2: 'building area 0 sf at the main grade level and a made-up overhang question'. I ran it with that test's house and spots plus steps = box(15,26,30,30,1.0,2.75,id='steps') against the front wall, main_building='f0'. At 7201d49 building_area gives readings [covered from above 810, at the main grade level 60] and the overhang question. At 7f8fca8 it gave 810 / 810 and read the value. front_yard also loses its 'to its walls at ground level' reading, because the main's section is empty and gets filtered out. It is still needs review, so not a false pass, but the at-grade number and the overhang question are both wrong. The fix handles the group's lowest member (the balcony case) but not the pattern: any member resting on the ground above the group's lowest bottom is erased.
evidence:
def _cut_level(building, buildings, plan_level):
    group = next((g for g in _connected(buildings) if any(b is building for b in g)), [building])
    return max(plan_level, min(_bottom(b) for b in group if b.get("faces")))
...
cut = ops.unary_union([_section(b, _cut_level(b, buildings, plan_level) + TOL) for b in buildings])
...
("to its walls at ground level", _section(main, _cut_level(main, buildings, plan_level) + TOL))) if not s.is_empty]
Run: house f0..f2 z0=2.75, spots [[22.5,29.5,1],[22.5,60.5,3],[9.5,45,2],[35.5,45,2]], steps box(15,26,30,30,1.0,2.75) -> at grade 60 sf (was 810).
pin: New test in packages/model_measurement/tests/test_measure.py: the round-5 slab house on its slope plus steps from 1.0 to 2.75 ft against its front wall. It asserts building_area value == approx(810) (or both readings 810) and that front_yard keeps a 'to its walls at ground level' reading. It must fail with the current _cut_level. Keep test_a_raised_balcony_on_flat_ground_keeps_the_overhang_question passing.
suggested_fix: Decide per solid, not per group, whether it rests on the ground. A solid whose bottom is at or below the ground under its own footprint (flat: grade + TOL; spot grades: the same ground _floating computes at its corners) is cut at max(plan_level, its own bottom). Only a solid raised off the ground (the balcony at 10 ft) is cut at the level of the ground-resting part of its group. Better still, cut each ground-resting member at its own bottom and leave raised members out.
skeptics:
The finding holds; I couldn't refute it.

What I read: measure.py:185-189 at 7201d49 matches the quote exactly. _cut_level returns max(plan_level, min(_bottom(b) for b in group)), where group is the solid's _connected group (measure.py:991-1001: solids touching in plan within TOL are grouped). Both callers use it: building_area at measure.py:1285 and the yard reading "to its walls at ground level" at measure.py:1313-1315, which drops empty sections.

So a touching solid that sits lower pulls the whole group's cut down to the grade plane. A house slab above that plane then gives an empty section. I found nothing upstream that stops this. A ground-level step or terrace against the house is an ordinary thing to model.

I ran the reviewer's exact scenario through measure(): the round-5 test house f0..f2 with z0=2.75, its spot grades, plus steps=box(15,26,30,30,1.0,2.75) and main_building='f0'.
- At 7201d49: the building_area readings are covered from above 810 and at the main grade level 60, plus the overhang question. The front_yard readings lose "to its walls at ground level".
- At 7f8fca8: 810 / 810, the value is read, and front_yard keeps the ground-level reading at 30.

Scope: the base 2865842 cut every solid at plan_level (line 1008 there), so this case was also wrong at the base. Both 7f8fca8 and 7201d49 are inside the branch range, so this is a regression within the branch: it undoes for this variant the fix that 7f8fca8 made and that test_a_slab_above_the_grade_plane_on_a_slope_is_cut_at_its_own_bottom pins. It ends in needs review, never a pass, so not a false pass. But the at-grade area and the overhang question are both wrong, which fits P2.

I could not refute this. I reproduced it myself. In measure.py:185-189, _cut_level returns max(plan_level, the lowest bottom of the whole connected group from _connected at measure.py:991). So when a lower solid touches the house, every member of the group is cut at that lower level, below the house's own slab. My setup used the house and spot grades from test_a_slab_above_the_grade_plane_on_a_slope_is_cut_at_its_own_bottom (tests/test_measure.py:1359), plus steps = box(15,26,30,30,1.0,2.75). I ran it at 7201d49 with the PYTHONPATH set to include rule_format. building_area came out value=None with readings [covered from above 810, at the main grade level 60] and the made-up overhang question. front_yard lost its 'to its walls at ground level' reading. I got this with main_building unset and with main_building='f0'. I ran the same script on a git archive of 7f8fca8 and got 810/810 with value 810.0, and the 'to its walls at ground level' reading was still there. So 7201d49's group-lowest cut brings back the round-5 slab-on-a-slope bug whenever a lower solid touches the house. The existing test still passes only because it has no lower solid touching the house. This is not a false pass, because the result stays needs review. But the at-grade area and the overhang question are wrong, as the finding says.

title: A count of 0 is now kept with no way to change it: the Stories row loses its Enter button and the plugin no longer rolls the 0 back
detail: f2c1347 swapped the 0-stories refusal from stories_below_floors ('fewer than the floor blocks drawn (1)') to the new stories_below_one ('fewer than one: every building has at least a first story (§325-3): check the count'). The plugin's undo in enter_rooms uses rhino_logic.refused_stories, which matches only 'fewer than the floor blocks drawn' or 'more than the drawing could hold'. So a 0 typed through Enter is saved and kept. The new reason also contains neither 'enter the number of stories' nor 'enter the count' (STORIES_ASKED), so stories_needed is False and the row drops its Enter button. needs_of leaves out 'stories', no hint is set, and the plugin has no other place to edit the stories count. The architect ends up with a Stories row stuck on needs review that says 'check the count' but gives no way to change it. That is a dead end, worse than the loop this round removed. The intent's own check ('Enter loop is gone on every path … 0') fails this way. I ran it: a 30 ft plain house with update_counts(base, {'stories': 0}) gives status needs_review, needs [], hint None, and refused_stories(view['items']) is None. At 7f8fca8 the same input gave 'The stories typed (0) are fewer than the floor blocks drawn (1)… The count wasn't kept.' and the 0 was rolled back.
evidence:
rhino_logic.py: refused = "fewer than the floor blocks drawn" in why or "more than the drawing could hold" in why
stops.py: "stories_below_one": "the stories typed ({typed}) are fewer than one: every building has at least a first story (§325-3): check the count"
gordium_rhino.py enter_rooms: refused = logic.refused_stories(...) if "stories" in answers else None; if refused: save_facts(doc, facts) ...
_count: gi.SetLowerLimit(0, False)  (0 is accepted)
update_counts accepts 0 ("0 or more").
pin: Add to test_the_stories_row_asks_for_the_whole_buildings_count_and_takes_it in packages/design_checker/tests/test_present.py: view = check_site(_plot(big), update_counts(base, {'stories': 0})). Assert logic.refused_stories(kept) is truthy and contains "wasn't kept". It must fail at 7201d49.
suggested_fix: Let refused_stories recognise every refusal of a typed count. Best is a marker from the measuring (for example refused_count=True on the _missing records for stories_below_floors, stories_above_drawn and stories_below_one) rather than matching words, so the plugin always rolls back the bad count and the Enter button comes back. Or have the Rhino prompt for stories refuse 0 (SetLowerLimit(1) for the 'stories' key), but keep the measuring's refusal for 0 that comes from a saved facts file.
skeptics:
I could not refute this. I read the code at 7201d49 and the finding is real.

- **How 0 reaches the new refusal.** In measure.py:714-722, a typed count checks stories_below_floors only when `counted` is not None. With no floor blocks drawn (a plain solid), `counted` is None, so a typed 0 falls through to `stated < least` (least = 1) and returns the new stories_below_one stop. The text of that stop is at stops.py:74-75.
- **The path is reachable.** Before anything is typed, a plain 30 ft solid gets the _decide reason "...draw its floors or enter the count (story)" (measure.py:729-732). That matches STORIES_ASKED, so present.py:858-861 adds 'stories' to the row's needs and the Enter button shows. The prompt allows 0: gordium_rhino.py:1371 has SetLowerLimit(0, False), and update_counts (rhino_logic.py:175-188) accepts 0 or more.
- **0 is kept.** After the save, enter_rooms (gordium_rhino.py:937-944) rolls back only when refused_stories returns a message. refused_stories (rhino_logic.py:148-153) matches only "fewer than the floor blocks drawn" or "more than the drawing could hold". I ran it on the stories_below_one reason and it returned None, so the 0 stays saved.
- **The Enter button disappears.** stories_needed (rhino_logic.py:143-145) also returned False on that reason, since it contains neither "enter the number of stories" nor "enter the count". So the row drops 'stories' from its needs. needs_of (rhino_logic.py:156-158) always leaves 'stories' out.
- **No other way to edit the count.** In the plugin, update_counts is called only from enter_rooms (gordium_rhino.py:937). I found no other place where the architect can change the stories count.
- **This is new on this branch.** At 2865842, the check in measure.py:646-647 has no `counted` guard, so a 0 hit stories_below_floors (or stories_below_blocks at :643). That reason matches refused_stories, so the 0 was rolled back.

Result: the Stories row is stuck on needs review, saying "check the count" with no Enter button. The regression is confirmed.

I couldn't refute this. The finding holds up in the code at 7201d49:
- measure.py:713-722: with a count typed and no floor blocks drawn (counted is None), 0 gets past the stories_below_floors check (713, which only runs when counted is not None) and past stories_above_drawn. It then hits `stated < least` with least=1 and returns stop("stories_below_one"). That stop key is new in this branch; it is not in stops.py at 2865842. test_measure.py:1400-1401 confirms that 0 on a plain 30 ft box gives this reason.
- stops.py:74-75: the reason says "...fewer than one: every building has at least a first story (§325-3): check the count". It contains neither "enter the number of stories" nor "enter the count".
- rhino_logic.py:140-145: stories_needed only matches those STORIES_ASKED phrases, so it returns False. present.py:858-861 therefore leaves "stories" out of needs, and needs_of (rhino_logic.py:157) always skips stories.
- rhino_logic.py:148-153: refused_stories only matches "fewer than the floor blocks drawn" or "more than the drawing could hold", so it returns None for the new reason.
- gordium_rhino.py:937-944 (enter_rooms): the facts are saved through update_counts, which accepts 0 (rhino_logic.py:175-188). They are only rolled back if refused_stories is set, so the 0 is kept.
- I searched gordium_rhino.py for any other way to set the stories count and found none. The only route is the row's "enter" button (684, 921), and it shows only when needs contains "stories".
- The path is reachable: a plain 30 ft house has a range of 1 to 4 stories. Its reason (measure.py:732, "draw its floors or enter the count") does show the Enter button, so an architect can type 0.
Result: the 0 is saved, the Stories row stays on needs review, its Enter button is gone, and nothing rolls the 0 back. The architect has no way to change the count. This regression comes from this branch, which added the stories_below_one key without updating refused_stories or STORIES_ASKED.
